rules.title: California Civil Code Section 1950.5 (security deposits)
rules.requirement: On transfer of the landlord's interest, the landlord must either transfer the remaining deposit to the successor or return it to the tenant with an accounting, and give the tenant notice. Successors are jointly liable for noncompliance, bad-faith retention may incur statutory damages of up to twice the deposit, and a lease may not call a deposit "nonrefundable."
rules.key_value: Statutory damages up to twice the amount of the security for bad faith
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages, for bad faith claim or retention
rules.status_basis: Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1 (AB 414), effective January 1, 2026; section is in the code.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental security deposits generally.

rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”
